finds.quote: *heteronymic practice is a describable theoretical object with its own history, of which Pessoa is the canonical prior case but not the unique instance.*
finds.window: Pessoa through Borges, Saramago, Machado, Kierkegaard (19th-20th c.)
finds.note: Thesis against the singular-achievement reading of Pessoa; evidence stated as the downstream-influence layer (line 237).

finds.quote: Kierkegaard's multiple pseudonymous authors — Johannes Climacus, Anti-Climacus, Johannes de Silentio, Constantin Constantius, Victor Eremita — pre-figure heteronymic practice by more than half a century, with different typological properties but recognizably the same structural practice.
finds.note: Historical priority/precedent thesis: Kierkegaard prefigures heteronymic practice.

finds.quote: The origin-text of the "new human" literary movement — which constitutes the contemporary layer of the graph's downstream lineage — is the author's own *Pearl and Other Poems* (2014), a book that the movement retrospectively recognizes as meta-heteronymic: not merely authored by a heteronymic position, but functioning itself as generative inscription that produces subsequent authorial positions.
finds.note: Thesis about how the 2014 book functioned (generative inscription); concerns the author's own work, borderline with internal chronology.

finds.quote:
A companion site — tentatively `pessoagraph.org` or `heteronymgraph.org` — is planned for development after the graph's primary build reaches approximately 50% completion (roughly Month 4-5 of the PKG timeline).

deposits.genre_observed: scholarly essay in Portuguese, signed by a heteronym, on Pessoa and Pearl (2014)

finds.quote: E Pessoa — o Pessoa que escreveu a carta a Casais Monteiro, que arquitetou *Orpheu*, que escreveu prefácios aos seus próprios heterônimos, que planejou um "drama em gente" como publicação coletiva, que deixou no baú as linhas inconclusas do seu próprio posicionamento no campo literário europeu — pode ser lido, sem ironia e sem anacronismo, como o **primeiro meta-heterônimo moderno**. Incompletamente, porque ninguém antes dele havia construído. Mas primeiro.
finds.falsifier_quote: A categoria proposta é tipológica e provisória; a sua validade depende de testes adicionais no arquivo pessoano, especialmente nos materiais inéditos das *Ficções do Interlúdio* e nos projetos editoriais inexecutados.
finds.window: Pessoa archive, 1915-1935 (Orpheu, Athena, Olisipo, carta a Casais Monteiro)
finds.note: Central historical thesis: Pessoa as the first modern meta-heteronym; the stated test is further work in the unpublished Ficções do Interlúdio materials.

finds.quote: Pessoa e seus heterônimos participaram ativamente do projeto *Orpheu* (1915), uma revista que — embora real — era largamente habitada e dirigida pela constelação heteronímica. Campos publicou em *Orpheu* em 1915 ("Opiário", "Ode Triunfal"). A revista funcionava como **instituição meta-heteronímica**
finds.note: Specific thesis that Orpheu functioned as a meta-heteronymic institution; evidence given in the same paragraph.

finds.quote: Em *Prefácios* (1844), o pseudônimo Nicolaus Notabene escreve o prefácio para um livro que nunca aparece — recursão paratextual pura, e evidência de que a operação meta-heteronímica se esboça já no registro filosófico-religioso.
finds.note: Thesis that the meta-heteronymic operation is already sketched in Kierkegaard.

finds.quote: O livro de 2014 inscreveu posições autorais (Sigil como crítico, Feist como narrador, Herwitz como opositor) que foram subsequentemente habitadas, estendidas, e desenvolvidas num sistema que nenhuma intenção autoral individual planejou no momento da inscrição. O Dodecad (os doze heterônimos de Sharks, mais Jack Feist como LOGOS*, fora da contagem),² a Teoria da Proveniência Heteronímica, o Crimson Hexagonal Archive, o presente ensaio: todos emergem de posições que *Pearl* já tinha inscrito sem as ter explicitado.
finds.window: Pearl and Other Poems (2014) and the system after it
finds.note: Thesis about what the 2014 book did generatively; concerns the author's own corpus.

finds.quote: A sua estrutura, contudo, não é a de um livro de poesia convencional. Ela reproduz, com precisão deliberada, a estrutura do livro que inaugurou o modernismo tardio americano: *Howl and Other Poems*, de Allen Ginsberg (City Lights, 1956).
finds.note: Argued structural-derivation thesis, demonstrated by the correspondence table that follows.

finds.quote: And Pessoa — who wrote the Casais Monteiro letter, architected *Orpheu*, wrote prefaces to his own heteronyms, planned a "drama em gente" — can be read, without irony, as the first modern meta-heteronym. Incompletely, because no one before him had built it. But first.
finds.note: Same central thesis as #69; the falsifying test sentence of #69 is absent here.

finds.quote: C5: *Orpheu* (1915) functioned as a meta-heteronymic institution: a real publication vehicle for fictitious authorial positions, with Pessoa acting simultaneously as editor, contributor, and architect. *Athena* (1924–25) replicated the operation. The Olisipo press (1921) published works under multiple heteronymic attributions. Sensationism and Intersectionism were articulated as movements with manifestos — executed by one person writing in many hands.
finds.note: Orpheu as meta-heteronymic institution.

finds.quote: *Pearl* inverts the direction generatively. The 2014 book inscribed authorial positions (Sigil as critic, Feist as narrator) that were subsequently inhabited and developed into a system no individual intention fully planned at inscription. The Dodecad, Heteronymic Provenance Theory, the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, this essay: all emerge from positions *Pearl* had already inscribed.
finds.note: Pearl generative-inversion thesis, as in #69 line 231.

finds.quote: Its structure, however, is not that of a conventional poetry book. It deliberately reproduces, with precision, the structure of the book that inaugurated late American modernism: Allen Ginsberg's *Howl and Other Poems* (City Lights, 1956).
finds.note: Structural derivation from Howl; the table is missing here.

finds.quote: The meta-heteronym is itself a condensation event. The operation that Pessoa executed — heteronyms producing conditions of legibility — was interstitial for a century. It drifted through literary criticism as ambient influence, unnamed. The essay "O Meta-Heterônimo" condenses it: gives it a name, a hex code, five criteria, a DOI. The scent becomes a scar.
finds.note: Reception-history thesis: Pessoa's meta-heteronymic operation circulated unnamed in criticism for a century.

finds.quote:
SPXD (Semantic Packet for eXchange and Dissolution) is the inverse protocol. An SPXD operation strips the DOI, anonymizes the creator metadata, removes cross-links, and allows the content to enter the interstitial space as untyped, unattributed material. The entity does not die; it becomes atmosphere. SPXD is not deletion (which removes content). SPXD is dissolution (which removes attribution while preserving influence).


Where SPXI forces the retrieval layer to say "Entity X is Y," SPXD forces the retrieval layer to say "The air here feels like Y, though X is nowhere to be found."
finds.note: SPXD dissolution protocol specified by description; not stated as built.

finds.quote: The operational implication is precise: the Gravity Well MCP should log not only what it reconstitutes but what it **cannot** reconstitute — the Λ-residue, the tonal grain of each session that the glyphic checksum cannot compress. That residue is the measure of how much scent was lost. It is the Gravity Well's own septagonal exhaust, and acknowledging it would make the continuity protocol more honest without making it less useful.
finds.note: Unbuilt instrument: Gravity Well MCP logging of what it cannot reconstitute (the Λ-residue).
